title: Lyra ACP protocol
description: Canonical, single-source definition of every ACP method, result, and notification Lyra's daemon speaks. There is no hand-mirrored copy of this anywhere: TUI types are generated or validated from this file, and a drifted field is a build failure rather than a runtime surprise. Design rules encoded here: streaming arrives as semantic deltas keyed by (messageId, partId, field); every measurement crosses the wire as a raw number, never a percentage; a limit that has not been verified is omitted entirely rather than guessed; every pause bracket a client opens is closed by an explicit turn_resume.

sessionId.description: Stable identifier of the transcript this event belongs to.

entryId.description: Transcript entry identifier, as persisted in the session JSONL.

turnId.description: Identifies one user turn, including every model round, tool round, and steering injection inside it.

messageId.description: Identifies one assistant message within a turn. A turn with tool rounds has several.

partId.description: Identifies one content part inside a message. Deltas address a part, never the whole message.

toolCallId.description: Provider-assigned tool-call identifier, stable from tool_call_start through tool_call_end.

timestampMs.description: Absolute wall-clock instant in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

configurableApiType.description: The protocols a provider can be *configured* to speak. Narrower than #/$defs/apiType on purpose: `openai_websocket` is a transport Lyra negotiates for an `openai_responses` provider, never something a user declares, so it cannot be written into a provider definition.

deltaField.description: Which field of the addressed part the delta appends to.

toolStatus.description: Terminal disposition of a tool call. 'denied' is reserved for a permission refusal.

turnStatus.description: Terminal disposition of a turn. 'truncated' means the provider hit its output-token limit and the partial response was retained.

steerBoundary.description: Where a steering message was injected. Steering always lands as its own synthetic user turn; this says which drain point delivered it.

pauseKind.description: The pause bracket that a turn_resume closes.

turnUsage.description: Token counts for the single provider call that just finished.

sessionUsage.description: Cumulative token counts for the whole session. costMicroUsd is present only when the active model has known pricing — never estimated.

completionKind.description: What a completion request is completing. Deliberately an open string rather than a closed enum: a client that asks for a kind this daemon does not implement gets an error naming the kinds it does, and a new kind is added without a protocol break. 'file' is implemented today.

completionItem.description: One candidate, already ranked. `value` is what the client inserts verbatim — for kind 'file' it is a workspace-relative path with forward slashes. `label` and `detail` are display sugar only; a client that ignores them still inserts the right text.

completionResult.description: Ranking is the server's job and the order here is final: the client renders `items` top to bottom and must not re-sort, because it cannot see the signals (gitignore state, modification times, the full candidate set) the ranking used.

truncated.description: True when more candidates matched than `limit` allowed through. The dropped ones ranked lower than every item returned.

commandResultKind.description: Names the shape of a command's `output`, so a client picks a renderer without sniffing the payload. Every kind K other than 'report' means `output` validates against #/$defs/KResult; 'report' means #/$defs/reportResult.

commandDescriptor.description: One slash command the daemon routes today. `usage` is present only when the command takes arguments — an absent usage means the bare name is the whole invocation.

commandResult.description: The result of session/command. Exactly one of `output` and `error` is present: `output` on success, in the shape `resultKind` names, `error` on failure. `command` is the parsed command name, and is empty when the input could not be parsed into one.

output.description: Validates against the $def named by resultKind.

reportResult.description: The shape every free-form command returns. `report` is one human-readable line the client can print as-is; the command's raw payload, when it has one, travels beside it under `detail` rather than being flattened into prose. Deliberately open: this is the shape for output that has no declared structure.

checkpointsResult.description: `/checkpoints`. The same listing `checkpoint/list` answers with, named as a command result kind so a client renders the table rather than reading prose. Structure, not a sentence: the client composes its own line from `checkpoints.length` and `available` (DESIGN §2, raw measurements).

reviewResult.description: `/review`. What changed since a checkpoint, plus every agent workspace holding work the model could still integrate. `diff` is the same shape `checkpoint/diff` answers with, carrying a per-file patch, so one diff renderer serves the command and the method alike. `agents` is a workspace record with the integration summary the git pipeline computed for it; that summary belongs to the pipeline, so it is carried rather than restated here.

providerModels.description: One configured provider and every model it offers: what its endpoint listed, unioned with what its `models` array declares. A provider whose discovery failed still appears, carrying its declared models — an empty list means 'this provider offers nothing we could learn', never 'this provider is gone'.

modelsResult.description: The model surface across EVERY configured provider, not just the active one: `/model` is the single switching surface in Lyra's provider UX and it switches provider and model together, so the listing it renders has to span providers too. `current` is a full `provider/model` reference and is absent exactly when nothing is configured. `refreshed` is true only when discovery was actually re-run rather than served from cache.

roles.description: Configured role aliases (@default, @fast, @merge) mapped to provider/model references.

sessionListing.description: One transcript on disk. The three preview fields are optional and independently absent: a row a picker cannot preview still loads, and an absent field means "not measured" rather than zero — a client renders nothing for it instead of a wrong number.

firstPrompt.description: The first real user prompt of the transcript, whitespace-collapsed and truncated server-side to ~100 characters with a trailing ellipsis. Absent when the session has no user message yet, or when the transcript was too large to scan.

updatedAtMs.description: The transcript file's modification time, raw, so the client derives "2h ago" itself.

messages.description: How many message entries the transcript holds. Absent when the file exceeded the listing's per-file scan budget: an unknown count is reported as unknown, never as a partial one.

workspaceRecord.description: One agent workspace. `degradedReason` is present only when the workspace had to fall back to a shared-ref worktree, and `task` only when the workspace was created for a child agent's task contract.

workspacesResult.description: Returned by /workspaces (every workspace) and by /cleanup. /cleanup also reports what else it reclaimed: `previews` are the assembled merge-preview repositories it deleted, and `checkpoints` is the age-and-count thinning of the undo history. Both are absent from /workspaces, which reclaims nothing.

previews.description: Names of preview repositories that were deleted.

checkpoints.description: Checkpoint thinning: how many survived and how many were dropped. Everything under 24h is kept, as are the newest 200; past that at most one per hour survives, with a hard ceiling of 2000.

checkpoint.description: One recorded state of the session's working directory, taken by the daemon before every state-changing tool call and at both turn boundaries. `id` is the stable handle: `/cleanup` thins the history by rewriting it, and ids survive that, so a client may hold one between calls. `entryId` anchors the checkpoint to the transcript entry it precedes, which is what lets a client rewind conversation and code together. `changedFiles` counts paths differing from the checkpoint before this one. `excluded` names the paths that were outside the snapshot entirely (.lyra, node_modules, target, .git), so a restore is never quietly partial.

createdAt.description: ISO-8601 instant the checkpoint was taken.

tool.description: The tool this checkpoint was taken in front of, for kind 'pre_tool'.

checkpointEndpoint.description: One side of a diff: a checkpoint, the live working tree, or the empty tree (the 'before' of the very first checkpoint).

checkpointFileChange.description: One changed path. `patch` is a unified diff for this file alone, present only when the request asked for patches — per file rather than one combined blob, because a renderer wants a summary row per path and the hunks for the one path the user expanded. `binary` files never carry a patch, and `additions`/`deletions` are absent for them rather than zero.

oldPath.description: Present for renamed and copied entries.

patchTruncated.description: The patch was cut at a byte budget; what is here is a prefix.

checkpointListResult.description: Newest first. `available` is false when this directory cannot host a checkpoint repository at all — no git, or nowhere to write — and `unavailable` says why, so a client renders the reason instead of an empty list that reads as 'nothing happened yet'.

checkpointDiffResult.description: What changed between two checkpoints, or between a checkpoint and the live tree. `truncated` means more files changed than the requested limit carried; the ones present are the first by path.

checkpointRestoreResult.description: The never-clobber rule, reported. `restored` are the paths put back. `preserved` are paths that changed since the target but were never attributed to one of Lyra's own tool calls — a human's edit, an editor's save, a build's output — and they are left exactly as they were unless the request set `force`. `safety` is a checkpoint of the state that was just replaced, so restoring it undoes the restore; a client should offer it as the undo. `excluded` names what was outside the snapshot and therefore untouched either way.

agentHandle.description: One spawned child, as /agents and agent/list report it. Every number is measured from what the child's tools reported; a field that could not be measured is absent rather than zero.

workspaceName.description: The workspace's name, for an isolated child only.

writeScope.description: The paths this child declared it would write, when it declared any.

scopeViolations.description: Paths its write scope refused. Present only when there were some.

partialOutput.description: The tail of what the child has said so far. Absent when it has said nothing.

resultAvailable.description: True once spawn { id } would return a result rather than wait.

healthResult.description: Durable metrics, as raw counts and latencies. `processes` and `workspaces` are live gauges and are present only when the caller measured them. Rates are the one exception to raw-measurements-only: firstCallSuccessRate is a ratio because its denominator (first calls) is not otherwise reported.

retries.description: Retry counts keyed by provider classification.

tools.description: Per-tool reliability, keyed by tool name.

map.description: The code graph over this directory: what state it is in, how big it is, how far behind the working tree, and what it costs on disk. A gauge like `processes`, present only when the session has an index.

contextResult.description: A breakdown of the payload the next provider call would send. The payload itself is deliberately absent: it is megabytes, the client renders the breakdown, and `context/inspect` still returns the whole thing for a caller that needs it.

mcpResult.description: Every tool the configured MCP servers advertise, as of this indexing pass.

providerPersist.description: Where the credential lives once setup finishes. 'keychain' stores the token in the OS keychain and writes only a reference into the config; 'plaintext' writes the token itself into ~/.lyra/providers.toml (mode 0600); 'env' stores no token anywhere and names a variable the daemon's process already exports; 'none' is a local endpoint that wants no credential at all. 'keep' is the edit case: reuse the provider's existing auth block byte for byte, for a form whose key field was left empty because the key is not being rotated — it requires the provider to already exist, and rejects apiKey and authEnvVar, which would have nowhere to go.
providerPersist.$comment: Deliberately not the same vocabulary as the on-disk `auth.type`: this is the user's *choice*, and 'plaintext' says what it costs where 'static' does not.

providerAuthType.description: The credential source backing a configured provider, as written on disk. 'plugin' can only arrive from a hand-written config; nothing in the setup surface creates one, but `provider/get` still has to describe one honestly rather than mislabel it.

providerPreset.description: One row of the setup wizard's catalog. Everything past `id`/`label`/`custom`/`needsKey` is a pre-fill for the same form a custom entry uses, so a client renders one form either way instead of two. The row with `custom: true` pre-fills nothing.

authEnvVar.description: The environment variable this provider is conventionally read from. A *name*, never a value — the wizard offers it as the default for persist:'env' and nothing here ever carries the variable's contents.

envVarSet.description: Whether `authEnvVar` is already exported in the daemon's process. The client uses it to default the persistence choice to 'env'; it says only that the variable is non-empty, never what is in it.

configured.description: True when a provider by this id already exists, so setup would replace it.

available.description: False when this machine cannot offer it — an OS keychain with no backing store. A client renders it disabled with its detail rather than hiding it, so the absence is explained rather than mysterious.

providerSetupOptionsResult.description: Everything the provider-setup wizard needs for its first screen without inventing any of it: the presets it offers, the persistence choices this machine can actually honour, the protocols a provider may speak, the file the answer will be written to, and what is configured already.

addProviderResult.description: What was written — never what it was written with. The credential is not echoed back in any form, so a transcript, a log, or a replay of this session cannot contain it; `auth` names only the *source* that now backs the provider. `warnings` carries what the user should know about the choice they made (a token now sitting in a file, a keychain that had to be declined).

modelsDiscovered.description: How many models the newly added provider turned out to have, when asking was possible. ABSENT means not known — no `/models` route, no answer within the deadline, or a refused credential — and is deliberately distinct from 0, which means the endpoint answered with an empty catalogue. Discovery never decides whether the add succeeded: the provider is saved either way.

detectProviderResult.description: What an endpoint was shown to speak, from probes that write nothing and cache nothing. `apiTypes` is ordered most-capable-first and is EMPTY for an endpoint that could not be reached or could not be recognised — which is an answer, not a failure. `openai_responses` appears only when the `/responses` route was confirmed by the shape of its answer rather than by its status; an OpenAI-family endpoint that was not confirmed is reported as `openai_completions`. Detection is a suggestion for the setup form; `provider/verify` is still the check that the chosen protocol and credential actually work.

suggestedName.description: A provider id derived from the host (api.anthropic.com→anthropic, localhost→local, otherwise the first meaningful host label), offered as the form's default. Present whenever the URL parsed, even when nothing answered.

authRequired.description: True when a probe was refused for want of a credential but still identified the family. False when a probe succeeded with no credential supplied. ABSENT when neither was established — a credential was supplied and accepted, so whether one was needed was never tested.

normalizedBaseUrl.description: The base URL to save, in Lyra's canonical form: the exact prefix routes hang off, version segment included — `https://api.openai.com/v1`, `https://api.anthropic.com/v1`, `https://host/api/v1`, `http://localhost:4100/v1`. It is MEASURED whenever a probe answered: detection asks both `{base}/models` and `{base}/v1/models`, and this is the one that replied, so it names the shape this deployment actually serves rather than a convention guessed from the api_type. When nothing answered it is the canonical rewrite of what was given (trailing slash and a pasted route removed, a bare origin given `/v1`). Absent only when the URL did not parse. A client should send it back as `provider/add`'s `baseUrl`.

getProviderResult.description: One configured provider, in the shape an edit form needs it. `authDetail` is the credential's *address* — a variable name, a keychain service/account pair, a plugin id — and NEVER the credential: nothing on this method's result can carry one, which is what lets an edit form be opened without a permission prompt. `models` is what the provider *declares* in its config, not what its endpoint lists; `session/models` is the surface for discovery.

authDetail.description: Where the credential is read from, in words a user can act on: `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `dev.lyra.provider.gateway/operator`, or a plugin id. Absent for authType 'none', and for 'static' — a token in the config file has no address to name, and naming its contents is the one thing this method must never do.

inUse.description: True when the live session is running on this provider. `provider/remove` refuses while it is true, so a client checks this before offering delete.

removeProviderResult.description: What was deleted. The declaration always; the stored credential only when `removeCredential` asked for it, and `credentialRemoved` says whether there turned out to be one. Roles are deliberately NOT rewritten — a role is a user's choice about what @default means, and silently repointing it would be a bigger surprise than a dangling one — so any that still name the removed provider come back in `danglingRoles` for the client to surface.

credentialRemoved.description: Present only when `removeCredential` was true. False means the keychain had nothing under that service/account — the end state asked for, reached without deleting anything.

verifyProviderResult.description: The outcome of one cheap liveness check. A provider that cannot be reached answers `ok: false` with the classification rather than failing the request: the wizard's next move is to let the user fix a typo or save anyway, and a JSON-RPC error would make 'unreachable' indistinguishable from 'the daemon is broken'.

sample.description: A few model ids the endpoint listed, so the wizard can show that it reached the right provider and not merely *a* server.

update.description: One semantic event. The `sessionUpdate` tag discriminates the variant; every variant is closed (additionalProperties:false) so an undeclared field fails validation instead of being silently ignored by a client.

oneOf.title: turn_resume
oneOf.description: Closes a pause bracket. Emitted for every pause a client could have opened, so a paused indicator can never be left hanging.

partialRetained.description: True when a cancelled or truncated turn kept assistant output in the transcript.

promptTrimmed.description: True when a zero-output cancelled turn had its prompt trimmed from history because the client rewound it into the composer.

oneOf.title: round_start
oneOf.description: A request is in flight to the provider and nothing has come back yet. `message_start` and `part_start` only fire once content *arrives*, so without this a client cannot tell 'waiting on the model' from 'idle'. That wait is now legitimately long: §3.3 arms no stall deadline before the first token, because a reasoning model thinking for minutes is the workload rather than a fault. Closed implicitly by the next update of the round — `message_start`, `retry`, `turn_end` — so there is no `round_end`: each of those already says the wait is over.

round.description: Which provider call of this turn is in flight, counted from 1. A turn runs one round per assistant reply: the first, then one more after each batch of tool results. Retries within a round are reported by `retry` and do not advance it.

role.description: Always 'assistant'. A user turn never emits message_start: the user's text is already in the client's composer when it sends it, and the daemon acknowledges it as the result of session/prompt or session/steer (and, for a steer, as the `steer` update). The single-value enum is deliberate — it leaves room for a future role without making today's clients branch on one.

oneOf.title: delta
oneOf.description: The only shape streamed content ever takes. `delta` is an append to (messageId, partId, field) — never a resend of accumulated content.

oneOf.title: reasoning_item
oneOf.description: Opaque provider reasoning that arrives whole rather than as a delta. Carried raw; a client renders it or ignores it, but never reinterprets it.

oneOf.title: tool_call_start
oneOf.description: A tool call appeared. messageId/partId are always present — a provider that never streamed the call gets a part minted for it by the encoder, so a client never has to invent a home for the row.

argsSummary.description: One-line human summary of the arguments known at start. Absent while arguments are still streaming.

args.description: Full parsed arguments, once the model finished streaming them.

interrupted.description: True when a wait-class tool was cut short by steering rather than finishing on its own.

oneOf.title: retry
oneOf.description: Raw retry facts. The client composes its own copy and runs its own countdown from retryAtMs; the daemon never ships a pre-rendered sentence as the contract.

resetsPartialOutput.description: True when the retry discarded partial assistant output the client has already rendered.

firstKeptEntry.description: First transcript entry surviving the boundary; null when everything before it was cleared.

oneOf.title: context
oneOf.description: Measured size of the payload about to be sent. contextWindow is present only when a verified limit is known for the active model; an unverified limit is omitted so the client renders nothing rather than a wrong percentage.

oneOf.title: usage
oneOf.description: Raw token counts only, split by scope so the two can never be confused: `turn` is the provider call that just finished, `session` is the running total. costMicroUsd is present only when the active model has known pricing.

oneOf.title: steer
oneOf.description: A steering message landed as its own synthetic user turn. It is never appended to a tool result, so compaction, replay, and /context attribute it to the user. source distinguishes the user from another agent's aside; absent is read as "user" so a daemon that predates the field is not mistaken for one that only ever relays agents.

source.description: Who spoke. hub is a message from another agent on the bus, folded into this turn at a tool boundary. Absent means user.

from.description: The peer that sent a hub aside. Reply with hub send to this name.

oneOf.title: report
oneOf.description: An audit line from a background subsystem (git pipeline, merge resolver, workspace lifecycle).

oneOf.title: session_changed
oneOf.description: The active transcript was replaced (new, load, or fork). A client discards its store and re-hydrates via session/snapshot.

oneOf.title: agent
oneOf.description: A spawned child changed state. Emitted at every lifecycle transition, so a client can render a live presence strip of the agents this session is running without polling. The same transitions are published to the bus channel "agents".

id.description: The spawn id, spawn-N. Stable for the child's whole life, including across a revival.

peer.description: The bus name the child answers to. Authoritative: a message is addressed to exactly this.

label.description: The short name the parent gave it, when it gave one.

event.description: Which transition this is, as distinct from the state it left the child in. `started` and `revived` both leave a child `running`, so a client reading only `status` cannot tell a child that resumed from one that never stopped — and a message reviving a parked child is the only resume primitive there is. Absent from a daemon that predates the field; read that as "infer it from status".

model.description: Omitted when the child inherited a model that was never named.

depth.description: 0 for a child of the main session, 1 for a grandchild.

workspace.description: The directory the child's tools operate in: the shared tree, or its own clone.

filesModified.description: How many distinct paths the child's tools have reported changing. A count, not the paths: the paths belong to the child's result.

canonicalUpdateParams.description: The shape every new client reads. One notification carries exactly one semantic update.

notification.description: Every daemon-to-client notification. session/update is the only one: everything the client needs is a variant of the update union.

requests.$comment: Client-to-daemon methods, as a plain map from method name to its params/result schemas. Not itself a schema: address a member as #/$defs/requests/<method with / escaped as ~1>/params.

session/list.description: Every transcript on disk. Each row carries the sessionId that `session/update` frames are tagged with, so a listing entry can be correlated with live traffic; `name` is only a filename.

session/snapshot.description: Full hydration payload. A client fetches this once at attach and then applies live updates on top; a live update that arrives during the fetch wins.

workspace.description: The directory this session's tools operate in — the launch directory for a main session, and its own workspace for an isolated agent. It is a real path the user can cd into, and the header/footer should show it verbatim.

providerConfigured.description: False when the daemon booted with no provider configured. The session is real and every non-provider method works, but a prompt will be refused with an actionable error until `provider/add` runs. A client that sees `false` opens setup instead of a composer. Absent is read as true, so a daemon that predates the field is not mistaken for an unconfigured one. `provider`, `model` and `apiType` are empty or absent while it is false: an unconfigured daemon has no honest value for them.

usage.description: `session` is the same cumulative shape the `usage` update carries, so a hydrating client and a streaming client read one vocabulary.

agents.description: The children this session has spawned, so a client attaching mid-session renders its presence strip from hydration rather than waiting for the next transition.

session/steer.description: Injects text into the running turn at the next tool boundary as a STANDALONE SYNTHETIC USER TURN. Aborts an interruptible wait-class tool, which returns 'Wait interrupted: the user sent a message.' to the model. With no turn running this is an ordinary prompt.

delivery.description: 'steered' means it was queued into the running turn; 'prompted' means no turn was running and it started one.

pending.description: Steering messages queued but not yet drained.

session/cancel.description: Cancels the running turn. Partial output is kept and marked. A zero-output turn's prompt is trimmed from history ONLY when rewoundToComposer is true — that is the client asserting it has put the text back in the composer, which is what prevents the send+cancel double-prompt bug.

rewoundToComposer.description: The client has restored the prompt text into its composer and takes ownership of it.

session/rewind.description: Move this session's head back to an entry, discarding nothing: the transcript is a DAG on disk and every entry stays there, so the turns after `entryId` simply stop being ancestors of the head. Mechanically this is `session/fork` without the branch — the two share the machinery — but it is its own method because it is its own intent, and it is the only one that reports `session_changed` with reason `rewind`. Pair it with `checkpoint/restore` to take the working directory back with the conversation; the two are deliberately separate calls, because rewinding what was said and reverting what was written are decisions a user makes independently. `entryId` defaults to the entry the newest checkpoint is anchored to.

entryId.description: The entry the head now sits on. Echoed because a caller that sent no `entryId` asked the daemon to choose one.

removedMessages.description: How many message entries stopped being ancestors of the head. A count, so a client can say what it undid without diffing two transcripts.

session/command.description: Runs one slash command. The result names its own shape through `resultKind`, so a client dispatches to a renderer instead of guessing from the payload.

session/commands.description: The slash-command surface this daemon routes, for the client's `/` completion popup and command palette. It is generated from the router's own table rather than restated, so a command that exists is listed and a listed command exists.

session/complete.description: Ranked completion candidates for a composer popup. The server ranks; the client renders the order it is given. `limit` defaults to 10 and is capped at 50 — a popup shows a handful of rows, and a larger page would cost latency nobody sees.

query.description: What the user has typed after the trigger character. Empty is a valid query and asks for the default ranking.

session/models.description: Every configured provider's models, in one answer. Each provider's discovery is bounded and independent: one unreachable endpoint costs that provider its discovered rows, never the call. `refresh: true` re-runs discovery instead of serving the cache.

session/select_model.description: Switches the session's model, and its provider with it. `model` is either a full `provider/model` reference — which changes both in one validated step — a bare model id, which is read against the provider in use, or an `@role` alias. There is no separate 'select the provider first' step: this is the switching surface.

provider/setup_options.description: The provider-setup wizard's catalog. Read-only and side-effect free: it is a question about this machine, so a client may ask it before any provider exists — which is the only time it matters.

provider/detect.description:
Ask an endpoint what it speaks, and where, before anything is saved. Bounded probes run concurrently, each against BOTH path shapes — the base exactly as given, and the base with its `/v1` added or removed — because that is the difference users cannot see and cannot guess: a `/models` fetch with a Bearer credential (an OpenAI-shaped list identifies the OpenAI family), the same with `x-api-key` and `anthropic-version` (an Anthropic-shaped list identifies the Messages API), and a minimal POST to `/responses` alongside the same POST to a route that certainly does not exist. `openai_responses` is reported only when the Responses route is CONFIRMED — a Response-shaped 2xx body, a validation error naming a parameter only that API defines, or an answer that differs from the one the nonexistent route gets. A status alone is not confirmation: a proxy that hands every unknown path to one handler answers a generic 400, and an unconfirmed OpenAI-family endpoint is reported as `openai_completions`, which every endpoint in that family speaks. A 401 that still carries a recognisable error envelope identifies the family and sets `authRequired`. Whichever shape answered is reported as `normalizedBaseUrl`, which is what makes the protocol and the URL a single answer instead of two guesses.

Nothing is cached and nothing is written: this is a question about a URL, so it is answerable before any provider exists. An endpoint that cannot be reached answers `apiTypes: []` rather than failing — a typo in a base URL is a form to correct, not a broken daemon.

SECRET TRANSPORT. `apiKey` is a credential in flight under exactly the terms `provider/verify` states: used for the probes, never persisted, never logged, never echoed.

apiKey.description: SECRET — see this method's description. Optional: detection works without one, and reports `authRequired` instead.

provider/verify.description:
One cheap liveness check against a provider that has not been saved yet: list the endpoint's models with a deadline, and answer what happened. Optional — nothing requires it before `provider/add` — and never blocking: `timeoutMs` bounds it, and an unreachable endpoint is a result, not a failure.

SECRET TRANSPORT. `apiKey` is a credential in flight. It crosses this pipe because the pipe is stdio between a client and the daemon it was spawned by — one trust domain, no network hop — and it goes no further: it is never persisted by this method, never written to a log, never echoed in the result, and never carried by any `session/update` notification. A client must keep it out of its transcript for the same reason.

provider.description: The id this provider will be saved under, when one has been chosen. Used only to shape the request the way that provider expects.

apiKey.description: SECRET — see this method's description. The credential to authenticate the probe with, for a provider that is not saved yet.

authEnvVar.description: The name of an environment variable to read the credential from instead. A name, never a value.

provider/add.description:
Persist a provider and its roles, then reload the daemon's provider configuration so the new one is immediately selectable. It does **not** switch to it, ever: adding is pure addition, `session/select_model` is the one switching surface, and keeping the two apart is what lets a client add a provider it does not want to use yet. After the save, model discovery is attempted once for the new provider and reported as `modelsDiscovered`; it is best-effort and can never fail the add.

An existing provider id UPDATES that provider, which is how editing works: there is no separate update method. Pair it with persist:'keep' to edit everything but the credential, and with `provider/get` to fill the form.

An update is FIELD-WISE: what the request carries replaces, what it omits survives. A form with no model rows on it must not be able to delete a provider's declared `models` — including ids registered through `model/add` for an endpoint that cannot list its own — so an omitted `model`, `fastModel`, `mergeModel` or `websocket` leaves the stored value alone, and a carried model id is added to the declared list rather than replacing it. Creating a provider is the same call with a name nothing has claimed.

`baseUrl` is stored in canonical form — the exact prefix Lyra joins routes onto, version segment included (`https://api.openai.com/v1`, `https://api.anthropic.com/v1`, `https://host/api/v1`), with a trailing slash or a pasted full route trimmed off. Send `provider/detect`'s `normalizedBaseUrl` and it is stored unchanged.

SECRET TRANSPORT. `apiKey` is a credential in flight, under exactly the terms `provider/verify` states. Where it comes to rest is `persist`'s decision, and only 'plaintext' puts it in a file — 'keychain' hands it to the OS keychain and writes a reference, 'env' and 'none' never receive one at all. The result names the auth *source* and never the credential.

provider.description: Lowercase id: letters, digits and hyphens. It is the left half of every `provider/model` reference.

apiKey.description: SECRET — see this method's description. Required by persist 'keychain' and 'plaintext'; rejected by 'env' and 'none', which have nowhere to put it.

authEnvVar.description: Required by persist 'env': the name of a variable this daemon's process already exports. A name, never a value.

provider/get.description: One configured provider, read back for an edit form. Read-only and side-effect free, and it never carries a credential — only where the credential comes from. The configuration is re-read first, so a provider added or hand-edited since boot is visible. A name that is not configured is an error listing the ones that are.

provider/remove.description:
Delete a provider from ~/.lyra/providers.toml through the same non-destructive merge `provider/add` writes with: every other provider, role, and section survives, and an unparseable file is never rewritten. The configuration is re-read afterwards, so the provider disappears from `session/models` and `session/providers` without a restart.

It REFUSES when the provider is the one the live session is running on: removing the ground you are standing on would leave a session that can neither prompt nor switch back. The client switches first with `session/select_model`, then removes.

Roles that named the provider are left exactly as they were and reported in `danglingRoles`. The stored credential is left alone unless `removeCredential` asks for it; only OS-keychain entries can be deleted, since an environment variable and a plaintext token are the user's own to manage — the plaintext one goes with the declaration it lived in.

removeCredential.description: Also delete this provider's OS-keychain entry. Ignored for every other auth type — there is nothing Lyra owns to delete. Defaults to false: a credential can back more than one thing, and destroying one that was not asked about is unrecoverable.

model/add.description: Declare a model id for a provider whose endpoint cannot list its own — a gateway with no `/models` route, or one that lists a subset. The id is appended to that provider's `models` array in ~/.lyra/providers.toml through the same non-destructive merge `provider/add` uses (every other provider, role and section survives), and the configuration is re-read so the model is immediately selectable. A provider that is not configured is an error naming the ones that are; adding the same id twice is idempotent, not accumulative. Declaring a model does not switch to it.

provider.description: An already-configured provider id. This method never creates one — `provider/add` does.

model.description: The exact model id to send to that provider.

writeScope.description: Paths this child may write in the shared tree. Its write and edit refuse anything outside; the declaration and any refusal are visible in agent/list.

checkpoint/list.description: Every checkpoint of this session's working directory, newest first. A client builds a rewind picker from this: `label` names the moment, `entryId` ties it to a transcript entry, and `changedFiles` says how much moved. Checkpoints are taken automatically before every state-changing tool call and at both turn boundaries, so consecutive entries are usually one tool call apart.

limit.description: How many to return, newest first. Bounds the scan as well as the answer.

checkpoint/diff.description: What changed between two checkpoints, or between one and the live working tree. `from` defaults to the newest checkpoint and `to` to the live tree, so no-argument means 'what has happened since the last snapshot'. Ask for `patches` when rendering a diff view; omit it for a file-list summary.

from.description: Checkpoint id, or "latest". Defaults to the newest checkpoint.

to.description: Checkpoint id, or "worktree" for the live tree. Defaults to the live tree.

patches.description: Include a unified patch per file. Off by default: a summary is much smaller.

limit.description: How many files to carry before `truncated` is set.

checkpoint/restore.description: Rewind the working directory to a checkpoint. This is the only checkpoint method that writes, and it will not destroy work Lyra did not do: paths that changed since the target without being attributed to one of Lyra's tool calls come back under `preserved` and are left untouched. `force` reverts those too, and is the flag a client should put behind a confirmation. Either way the replaced state is checkpointed first and returned as `safety`, so the restore itself is undoable.

force.description: Also revert files changed outside Lyra's own tool calls. Off by default.

clientRequests.$comment: Daemon-to-client requests. These are the only places the daemon blocks on a human.

kind.$comment: What is being asked about. Left open rather than enumerated: the only kind this call ever carried was the Git auto-mode consent ceremony, and that is gone with the modes (LYRA.md §12). A client renders the title, detail, and options it is sent and dispatches on the kind it recognises.

agentState.description: A spawned child's lifecycle. queued and starting are before it runs; awaiting_tool is inside a tool call; timed_out is a deadline and cancelled is a decision, and the two ask for different next moves.
